wave: REPRESENT-PROGRESSIVE-1: extent as a selection dimension
forecast: represent-progressive-1.json (frozen before implementation; the four boundaries and the implementation order added as a dated addendum, also before code; neither edited afterwards)
status: BUILT 2026-09-06 — all nine steps of the implementation order pass, and P6's external-crate arm with them. No timing claim of any kind; the performance lane stays paused.

built.codec: `F32_PLANES` (family `F32_PLANES`, revision 1), registered in the built-in registry: an f32 image cut into three byte planes — `base_hi16` (the high half of the bit pattern, explicit little-endian), `refine_8a`, `refine_8b`. Three extents at 16 / 24 / 32 bits per weight; the planes PARTITION the pattern, so the terminal extent is the source bit for bit by construction. No direct realization: it executes through the mandatory canonical decode.
built.vocabulary: `StreamRole::Refinement { depth }` — the first extension the stream vocabulary has needed. `RepresentationCodec::streams_at(extent)` derives the streams an extent reads from the declared roles, so a loader opens exactly those without knowing what any stream means.
built.conformance: `represent/codec/conformance.rs`: `certify(codec, operands, shape, source, tensor)` decodes every declared extent, measures relative RMS against the SOURCE over the certified domain (finite normals), and refuses three ways — `CertificateViolated`, `CertificateNotMonotone`, `TerminalNotExact`. A declaration is now checkable by anything, not only by this codec's own tests.
built.loader: `OperandStore::load_at(operand, extent)` binds streams by DECLARED NAME: the first from the operand's own tensor, each further one from a sibling named `<tensor>.<stream>`. It opens only the streams the extent reads. `OperandStore::stored_len` now sums those siblings, so the footprint is every plane the container holds whatever extent is pinned.
built.pin: `RealizationRecord.extent: ExtentPin { selected, options }` — the pin carries the depth, never the semantic plan, which stays representation-independent. `ExtentOption` pairs each certificate with what that extent reads. `RegisteredFacts.extents` copies the codec's declaration out like its other declarations.
built.requirement: `RepresentationFloor::{Exact, RelativeRms(f64)}` on `ResidencyBudget` (default `Exact`), stated without naming a codec or a depth. An extent with no declared radius is admissible only as the terminal one: an undeclared error is not a small one.
built.accounting: `Resources`/`ResourceLedger`/`Expectation` gain `read_to_prepare` — stored bytes OPENED to prepare an operand at its pinned extent, aggregated once per stored operand like the footprint. `ResidencyBudget.prepare_bytes` bounds it and `BudgetDeficit.prepare` reports the overshoot.
built.selection: `select_realizations_within` answers a preparation deficit by taking a shallower extent the floor admits, one step at a time, largest saving first, recorded as a switch with the depths it moved between and marked `SelectionReason::BudgetPolicy`. Realization moves still answer physical and throughput deficits; the two kinds do not overlap, because a realization change moves what is HELD and an extent change moves what is OPENED.
built.closure: `opplan/build.rs::auxiliary_stream_of` gives a stream stored apart a fate: a tensor whose name extends another tensor's whole name by one dot-separated segment is accounted to that base rather than reported as an unclassified operand. The planner recognises only the SHAPE of the relationship; the loader, which holds the registry, checks that the suffix names a declared stream.

witnesses.codec_local: `represent/codec/tests/f32_planes.rs` (10 tests): the plane order read off a pattern with four distinct bytes; every extent stored at its declared width; the terminal extent reproducing 14 adversarial bit patterns exactly (both zeroes, both subnormal ends, both infinities, three NaNs, four-distinct-byte normals), compared as bit patterns; truncation toward zero with monotone error inside each declared radius; the certificate checked against the source; an OVERCLAIMING codec — same bytes, depth 0's radius declared as depth 1's — refused by depth and number; the edge semantics named one by one; a depth reading only its own planes and refusing a missing one; exact per-stream lengths with the compensating mutation (base one byte short, refinement one byte long) refused; a row range at every extent being that slice of the whole.
witnesses.container_level: `opplan/exec/tests/f32_planes_execution.rs` (5 tests): a depth opening exactly d+1 payloads on the store's own read counter; a shallow extent decoding from a container that does NOT hold the deeper plane, while the terminal extent refuses naming the missing tensor; each extent closer to the source than the one before it; the three selection arms; and a floor finer than any shallow extent leaving only the terminal one.
witnesses.contract_universals_restated: Two tests asserted things that were true of the codecs implemented rather than of the contract, and a progressive codec makes them false: `streams[0] == VALUES` (the shared spec, by NAME) became 'the first declared stream carries the values ROLE', and 'every codec declares exactly one extent, at depth 0, with no radius' became 'every codec declares its extents from the base up, contiguous, costing more and certifying at least as much with depth' plus a separate test naming the one progressive codec and requiring a radius per extent from it and none from the terminal ones. Restated, not patched.
witnesses.external_crate: `crates/larql-vindex/tests/external_progressive_provider.rs` (2 tests): an out-of-tree progressive codec registered through exported API alone, executing bit-exactly at its terminal extent, its extents reaching selection, and a budget plus a floor pinning its base extent — with the same budget refused under the default floor.

predictions_scored.P1: HELD. The trait's existing signatures took a progressive codec unchanged. Two PROVIDED methods were added (`terminal_extent`, `streams_at`), both derived from declarations the trait already had — an addition, not a change of shape.
predictions_scored.P2: FALSIFIED, and usefully. The forecast named two blockers (binding by declared name, a per-extent length rule) and predicted no third. A third appeared: the planner's closure pass reported every sibling plane as an `UnclassifiedOperand`, so a container holding streams apart could not be PLANNED at all, let alone loaded. Fixed by `auxiliary_stream_of`. The lesson is the one the wave was for: 'streams stored apart' is not only a loader concern — every pass that enumerates a segment's tensors has an opinion about them.
predictions_scored.P3: HELD, with the generalisation the addendum anticipated: no new selection ALGORITHM, but the greedy loop now answers the dimension in deficit rather than `resident` unconditionally. Extent moves are scored on bytes opened; realization moves on resident bytes. No quality optimiser was needed or built.
predictions_scored.P4: PARTLY FALSIFIED — the interesting result of the wave. The forecast said touch and page-in scale with the extent while resident and stored do not. In this codebase `touch_per_token` is priced from the RESIDENT IMAGE (the bytes the executor streams once an operand is resident), so under canonical decode it does not move with depth either: an f32 image is an f32 image at every depth. Nothing in the ledger moved with the extent, because the ledger had no dimension for what an extent actually changes — the stored bytes OPENED to prepare. That dimension (`read_to_prepare`) is now in the vocabulary, and the accounting witness asserts the whole shape: stored footprint unchanged, resident unchanged, touch per token unchanged, bytes opened strictly down.
predictions_scored.P5: HELD. No file under `exec/` outside `tests/` changed for execution: the loader and the accounting changed, the executor did not, and a decode at any extent returns the same shape.
predictions_scored.P6: HELD. `crates/larql-vindex/tests/external_progressive_provider.rs` — a separate crate in cargo's model, seeing only exported API — registers `PLANES16`, its OWN progressive representation (two planes rather than three, its own stream names, its own radius, deliberately not the shipped codec). The candidate container executes bit-identically to the f32 control at the terminal extent; the provider's two extents reach the pin priced from its own declaration; a preparation budget under a floor that admits its base extent moves the pin and lowers what is opened, while the same budget under the default floor is refused. No file under `src/` was edited for it: no match arm names the label, and the loader opens its second stream because the codec declares a refinement.

findings.PR1-N1: `RepresentationExtent::TERMINAL` was depth 0 — a name that read correctly while every codec had exactly one extent and generalised backwards: a progressive codec's terminal extent is its DEEPEST. Renamed to `BASE` (47 call sites), with `RepresentationCodec::terminal_extent()` for callers that mean 'the whole representation'. Three of those call sites meant the whole representation and now say so; the rest meant depth 0.
findings.PR1-N2: A shallow extent's value depends on the REALIZATION, not on the representation: under canonical decode it saves only what is read at preparation, because the decoded image is f32 whatever the depth. A direct realization over the planes — not built here — would make it save resident bytes too. This is the four-plane thesis in the small, and it is why `read_to_prepare` had to exist before selection could move a depth for a reason.
findings.PR1-N3: The certified domain is a real boundary, not a caveat. Truncation flushes a small subnormal to zero (unbounded relative error) and turns a NaN whose payload lives only in an omitted plane into an INFINITY of the same sign — the one case where the pattern's class changes. Both are named in the codec's documentation and pinned by tests, the radius certifies finite normals only, and `Domain::of_base_plane` reads how many elements are outside it from the base plane alone, without opening a deeper one.
findings.PR1-N4: A total-length rule cannot catch a compensating mutation. `lyrw2::bind_region` checks that the bound streams total `stored_bytes(terminal)`, which a base plane one byte short and a refinement one byte long satisfy exactly. The progressive codec validates per stream, per extent, and a test moves the byte to prove the difference.
findings.PR1-N5: A pre-existing shared-state race in the V4 stage instrument's own test surfaced under this wave's added tests, and is named here rather than re-run away. `stages::LEDGER` is a PROCESS-WIDE static; `exec/tests/stages_and_routing.rs` guards it with a mutex that only the three tests in that module take, so any other test in the binary that opens a `Stage::Router` timer can bump the counter inside the window — `a_stage_records_its_extent_and_a_reset_clears_it` read `calls == 2`. It passes alone and passed on the previous head; nothing in this wave opens a stage timer, so what changed is scheduling, not semantics. Left UNFIXED deliberately: the instrument belongs to the paused performance lane and produced V4's published split, so changing it without re-measuring is not this lane's call. The fix when that lane resumes is thread-local tallies — which would also close the latent measurement bug behind the flake, since a stage split is supposed to describe ONE execution rather than whatever else the process is timing.
